description: ACI pilot scenario: a single ACI fabric with Kubernetes (Cilium) nodes and VMs. Entity and traffic facts only; event formats come from the TA/product schemas cited in tools/gen_raw_fixtures.py and fixtures/raw-aci/FIELDS.md. Addresses: RFC 1918 internal, RFC 5737 for management and external hosts.
assumptions: Single ACI fabric aci-1 (APIC apic1 192.0.2.50, pod 1): leaves leaf-101/102/103, spines spine-201/202, each leaf eth1/49 -> spine-201 and eth1/50 -> spine-202.

Tenant shop, VRF prod, policy control enforcement ingress. Traffic entering an EPG port is classified by that EPG; traffic entering an L3Out is classified by source prefix (ExtEPG l3extSubnet, import-security); destinations that are endpoints classify by their EPG, other destinations by longest-prefix ExtEPG.

node-a and node-b are endpoints in EPG k8s/nodes (Cisco 'basic' design). node-c attaches through the floating-SVI L3Out k8s-bgp on leaf-103 (Cisco 'advanced' design), so it is not an fvCEp; its leaf port is known only from LLDP. Its address 10.10.22.13 is in the L3Out SVI subnet 10.10.22.0/24, because an L3Out SVI subnet cannot overlap bd-nodes 10.10.20.0/24 in the same VRF.

Cilium 1.20: routingMode native, kubeProxyReplacement true, ipv4NativeRoutingCIDR 10.0.0.0/8, bpf.masquerade true (traffic to destinations outside 10.0.0.0/8 is masqueraded to the node IP), loadBalancer.mode snat with bpf.lbModeAnnotation true and loadBalancer.dsrDispatch ipip (cart-api opts into DSR via service.cilium.io/forwarding-mode: dsr), LB IPAM pool 10.50.0.0/24, BGP control plane advertising LoadBalancer VIPs and pod CIDRs to L3Out k8s-bgp, Hubble static exporter writing /var/run/cilium/hubble/events.log with default monitor aggregation (medium).

With default monitor aggregation Hubble emits the post-translation TO_ENDPOINT flow at the backend; a SNAT forwarding trace (TO_NETWORK with IP.source_xlated) is present for c3a and c6 and absent for c3b, to exercise both attribution rules.

Cilium Gateway: Gateway shop (class cilium) creates Service cilium-gateway-shop with a dummy EndpointSlice 192.192.192.192:9999; Envoy on the receiving node proxies upstream from the node's ingress IP (Node annotation network.cilium.io/ipv4-Ingress-ip). Envoy emits no OTel spans; Hubble L7 flows carry X-Forwarded-For and trace context.

Cilium Ingress: Ingress shop/shop-www (ingressClassName cilium, ingress.cilium.io/loadbalancer-mode: dedicated) creates Service shop/cilium-ingress-shop-www with label cilium.io/ingress=true and a dummy EndpointSlice 192.192.192.192:9999; Envoy behaves as for the Gateway.

ACI NetFlow v9 exports from each leaf's OOB address to Splunk Stream, with monitors on the node, client and DB bridge domains and on the L3Out interfaces; records carry the ingress interface only. Nexus Dashboard Insights monitors site aci-1.
Contract subjects of win-to-shop and win-to-nodeports, and the deny subject of win-deny-db, use directives=log, so ACL-log records exist only for those.

conversations.summary: VM -> Cilium Gateway VIP; Envoy on node-a proxies two HTTP requests (to frontend on node-b and on node-a).
frontend on node-a calls checkout on node-b (cross-node pod traffic on the fabric).
frontend on node-b calls checkout on the same node; never reaches the fabric.
VM -> checkout-api LoadBalancer VIP (externalTrafficPolicy Local); only node-b hosts checkout, so only node-b advertises the VIP and the client IP is preserved.
checkout (node-b), serving the c2 request, -> orders-db-01 VM on leaf-102; pod source IP preserved (inside ipv4NativeRoutingCIDR).
VM -> Cilium Ingress (dedicated mode) VIP lands on node-b; Envoy on node-b proxies to the frontend pod on the same node (upstream never reaches the fabric).

access.route: Ingress shop/shop-www (class cilium) host www.shop.example.internal -> frontend:8080

conversations.summary: VM -> catalog-api VIP (Cluster, SNAT) lands on node-a; node-a SNATs to its IP towards catalog on node-c. Hubble forwarding trace present.
Same Service, another connection; Hubble emitted no forwarding trace (default monitor aggregation). Exactly one node-a -> catalog flow within one second.
VM -> cart-api VIP (Cluster, DSR via IPIP) lands on node-b; node-b encapsulates to node-c; cart replies directly from node-c with the VIP as source (asymmetric).
VM -> node-a:30080 (NodePort, Local); payment runs on node-a.
payment calls an external API; Cilium masquerades the pod IP to node-a's IP (destination outside ipv4NativeRoutingCIDR). Isovalent sees the pod IP; the fabric sees node-a.
VM -> node-b:30081 (NodePort, Cluster, SNAT) -> catalog on node-c; Hubble forwarding trace present.
VM -> frontend pod IP 10.42.1.15:8080 directly (pod CIDR advertised by Cilium BGP).
VM tries orders-db-01:5432 directly; the deny-with-log subject of contract win-deny-db drops it at leaf-103. Seen only as acllogDropL3Pkt.

traces.note: c1 request 1 via Cilium Gateway (Envoy, no spans) to frontend on node-b
c1 request 2 via Cilium Gateway to frontend on node-a, which calls checkout on node-b
c2 via checkout-api LoadBalancer (Local keeps the client IP); checkout writes to orders-db
c1d via Cilium Ingress (Envoy on node-b, no spans) to frontend on node-b
